name: ACP
description: Any Agent Client Protocol agent (Zed's ACP: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio), mapped onto the runner protocol. Google's Gemini CLI (`gemini --experimental-acp`) is the preset, its handshake verified; other ACP agents run through a custom command. Nothing stages the gemini binary into the colony image yet. Questions ride session/request_permission, file paths resolve inside the workspace, and terminal commands are only started with a workspace cwd.

requires.image: glibc + node >= 20 + the pinned @google/gemini-cli on PATH (npm install -g @google/gemini-cli) for the gemini preset

agent.title: ACP agent
agent.description: Which ACP agent to launch. `gemini` is the verified one: Google's Gemini CLI in its ACP mode (`gemini --experimental-acp`), authenticated with the GEMINI_API_KEY secret for generativelanguage.googleapis.com. `custom` launches any other ACP agent through the command below — declare its API hosts and credential in your deployment, since this manifest only declares Gemini's.

command.title: Custom command
command.description: Used when the ACP agent is `custom`: the full command line including arguments, e.g. `grok agent stdio` (unverified) or `node /opt/acp-agent/main.js --stdio`. Quote spans with single or double quotes to keep arguments with spaces whole.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model id meant for session/set_model after session/new. Not applied yet: the runner does not read this setting, so the agent runs on its own default model. Switching the model on a running colony works when the agent advertises model selection at session/new; otherwise it is a logged warning.

exec_policy.title: Exec policy
exec_policy.description: JSON exec policy this install layers over the built-in one: {"rules": [{"id", "decision": "deny"|"ask"|"allow", "reason", "command"|"script"|"touches"|"writes_outside"}]} (see modules/agents/acp/README.md). A matched rule answers session/request_permission for the command tool calls it names: allow approves the call without asking you, deny refuses it, ask becomes a question to you. Layers can only narrow: the built-in deny rules always hold, an org policy (COLONIZER_EXEC_POLICY_ORG) narrows further, and a repository's own .colonizer/exec-policy.json narrows further still. Empty uses the built-in policy alone.
